stops.name: Rector's Palace, Dubrovnik
stops.en: Artifacts, paintings and furniture dating from the time of the Dubrovnik Republic.

stops.name: Lovrijenac
stops.en: The monumental fort rises above 37 m high rock. It was an essential fortification for defence of the city from both ground and sea attacks. In order to prevent mutiny by the commander of the fortress, the walls facing the city are only 60 cm thick compared to those exposed to enemy fire which were 12 m thick. Above the entrance to the fortress is an inscription that says "Non bene pro toto li

stops.name: St Blaise's Church
stops.en: Baroque Church dedicated to the city's patron saint.

stops.name: Pile Gate, Dubrovnik
stops.en: A convenient starting place for a stroll through the Old Town.

stops.name: Dubrovnik Cathedral
stops.en: This impressive building is in the Poljana Marin Držić. Supposedly, the original church was built with money donated by Richard the Lionhearted who survived shipwreck on his way home from the Third Crusade. The current Roman Baroque cathedral dates from the 18th century.

stops.name: Franciscan Church and Monastery
stops.local: Franjevački samostan i crkva u Dubrovniku
stops.en: Houses artifacts from one of the world's oldest pharmacies.

stops.name: Dubrovnik Synagogue
stops.en: This synagogue built by Sephardic Jews is supposed to be the second-oldest still in use synagogue in Europe today. A permanent Jewish community here was founded at the end of the 15th century following the expulsions from Portugal and Spain. The Jewish Ghetto was established in 1546 on Jewish Street in the old town of Dubrovnik. The community flourished and included respected doctors, merchants an

stops.name: Onofrio fountain
stops.en: In the western (Pile) entrance of the old town, The fountain stairs are nowadays a favourite meeting place for local youth and where both the tourists and pigeons take rest and refresh themselves with cool water.

stops.name: Clock tower
stops.en: On top of the tower are the famous 'Zelenci' (The Green Ones), bronze statues which strike the gigantic bell every hour. They have been replaced with copies and the originals are in the atrium of the Sponza Palace.

stops.name: Saint Ignatius Church
stops.en: Ornate Jesuit church, approached via a romantic baroque staircase modelled on the Spanish Steps in Rome (1738). Built between 1667 and 1725 by architect Ignazzio Pozzo, and like most Jesuit churches of the period was modelled on the Gesù in Rome, the mother church of the Jesuits.

stops.name: Orlando's Column
stops.en: A slender stone flag staff of the legendary knight. Also known as Orlando's Column. Ever since its foundation in 1950, the Dubrovnik Summer Festival is opened by raising a flag carrying the city's motto Libertus on Orlando's staff.

stops.name: Dominican Church and Monastery in Dubrovnik
stops.local: Dominikanski samostan i crkva u Dubrovniku
stops.en: Paintings and artifacts from Dubrovnik's past.

stops.name: Maritime Museum
stops.en: Considering how vital sailing and shipbuilding were to the growth of the Dubrovnik Republic, this is one of the city’s most important museums.

stops.name: Natural History Museum (Dubrovnik)
stops.en: The collection of 100 year-old taxidermy specimens dates back to 1872 and may not appeal to everyone.

stops.name: Dubrovnik West Harbour
stops.en: A peaceful little gem where people swim, sunbath, canoe, and have coffee. When you walk up the stairs to the fort to the small forest, you have nice views on the city (not as nice as you would have from the fort itself, but €15 cheaper).

stops.name: Old Port
stops.en: The eastern part of the Old Town of Dubrovnik; some cruise ship passengers are tendered to the Old Port.

stops.name: Church of St. Sebastian
stops.en: 15th-century church built by the Ploče gate since St. Sebastian is the saint protector against plague.

stops.name: Serbian Orthodox Church and Museum of Icons
stops.en: Built from 1865-1877, stands behind impressive wrought iron gates. Houses a number of icons, mainly Byzantine and Cretan. Museum next to church has extensive icon collection.

stops.name: City Walls
stops.en: There are 3 entrances: the main entrance on Stradun inside the Pile gate, by Fort Saint John’s, and at the Customs House gate.

stops.name: Bukovac House
stops.en: Includes works by Vlaho Bukovac (1855-1922), one of the most famous modern Croatian painters. Part of the house is devoted to exhibitions of works by young artists.

stops.name: The Treasury of Cathedral
stops.en: The Treasury has 138 reliquaries which are carried around the city during the Feast of St Blaise.

stops.name: Home of Marin Držić
stops.en: Memorial house of Marin Držić, a famous 16th-century Croatian playwright from Dubrovnik.

stops.name: The Ethnographic Museum
stops.en: Built in 1590, this is a fascinating building, and the exhibits showcase the economic, cultural and spiritual development of Dubrovnik. The folk costumes and textiles give the best flavour of the region where folk culture is still celebrated.

stops.name: War Photo Limited
stops.en: An exhibition centre of war and conflict photography. Exhibits change during the season. Stunning images by world-renowned photo journalists.

stops.name: Lapad Beach
stops.en: A car-free, sandy beach area on the Lapad Peninsula, approximately 3.5 km from the old town, where you can relax in the shade of the numerous trees. At the end of a long pedestrianised street full of café bars and restaurants you will see many popular pebble beaches known as Lapad beaches. These beaches are really beautiful and well used. Lapad is definitely one of the most beautiful parts of Dubr

stops.name: Banje Beach
stops.en: A well-located pebble beach. There's a concessioned part with an entrance fee, but also a public part which is always livelier and more relaxed. Great way to beat the heat in the middle of the town. Amazing view of the city walls, Old Town Dubrovnik and the island of Lokrum. Beach volleyball, mini football or water polo. You can also enjoy lying on deck chair and having a drink.

eats.name: Buffet Škola
eats.note: Quaint, quick dinner! Delicious prosciutto, cheese, and salad. Excellent sandwiches. Freshly produced and the bread is a reminiscent of focaccia.

eats.name: Barba
eats.note: Great sea street food, big portions, nice and friendly staff. Even it is full inside, you can order take away, sit on the steps in front of the restaurant and eat, while looking at the streets of King

eats.name: Pizzeria Tabasco
eats.note: Decent and hearty pizza. Service is excellent and very sincere. Situated underneath the cable car system boarding point just near the walls of the old town.

eats.name: Pizzeria La Luna
eats.note: Large portions. Really good pizza with fresh ingredients. Only pizza is served before 17:00, for pasta or other dishes come later. 2Good pizza, friendly staff but service can be slow.

eats.name: Konoba Tabak
eats.note: Great food if you want to have a real taste of fresh fish & local food. A hang-out for the locals.

eats.name: Pizzeria Asterix & Obelix
eats.note: Typical roadside pizzeria. Correct quality. Nice place, close to the beach.

eats.name: Mea Culpa
eats.note: One of the best pizzerias on what is becoming a 'pizza street'. Go for pizza or a coffee and brandy and exchange banter with the staff.

eats.name: Nishta
eats.note: Dubrovnik's only vegetarian restaurant, with vegan and gluten-free options available upon request.

eats.name: Poklisar
eats.note: Limited but good menu, including pizza and some very enjoyable live piano music.

eats.name: Pizzeria Scala
eats.note: A very nice pizzeria between Lapad and Babin Kuk with good pizza and very good Mexican food/specialities.

eats.name: Spaghetteria Toni
eats.note: A small Italian-style restaurant in the old town with outdoor seating providing a wide variety of pasta.

eats.name: Lady Pi-Pi
eats.note: Worth the climb for magnificent views over the old town from the restaurants' terrace and presumably taking its name from an ancient water feature just outside the restaurant (not for the prudish). Gr

eats.name: Arka
eats.note: Dalmatian cuisine in an excellent location. Has some good vegetarian options. The baked moussaka especially is worth a try.

eats.name: Domino Steak House
eats.note: One of the best for a variety of ways of serving steak. Also serves traditional Dalmatian fare.

eats.name: Dubravka 1836
eats.note: Variety of pizzas, meat and seafood dishes, quality domestic and foreign wines, cocktails, homemade ice cream and desserts.

eats.name: Marco Polo
eats.note: Good traditional food served in a small outdoor courtyard. Really nice restaurant with different types of food.

eats.name: Proto
eats.note: Good seafood.

eats.name: Taj Mahal
eats.note: Offers a variety of Bosnian and Eastern cuisine such as Cevapcici u lepinji, baklava and tufahi. The wait can be quite long, and vegetarian options are often sold out.

eats.name: Gil's Little Bistro
eats.note: Friendly place for a mid-town meal.

eats.name: Lokanda Peskarija
eats.note: Temporarily closed as of May 2022. Traditional Dalmatian appetizers and meals, you get your meal in a large black fisherman's style pot.

eats.name: Nautika
eats.note: Great views of the sea and Old City. Pay attention to the menu prices which switch from kuna to euro throughout.

eats.name: Porat Restaurant & Terrace
eats.note: Spacious terrace, just outside the Pile gate. Offers international and Croatian cuisine.

eats.name: Cafe Buža
eats.note: The tables and chairs are set out on the side of the cliff and the beers are served in bottles and plastic cups. You can sunbathe on the rocks or do some cliff-diving but do watch for rocks below. Thi

eats.name: Casablanca
eats.note: Look for flashing red and blue lights. This is an interesting, slightly bizarre bar with seating outside on the city stairs, techno music, and may have erotic dancing.

eats.name: D'vino Wine Bar
eats.note: A selection of over 100 fine domestic and imported wine available by the glass, bottle, and in tasting servings. Largest selection of wines by the glass in Dubrovnik with a very intimate, romantic atm

eats.name: NoneNina
eats.note: Chill music fills this lounge bar at night, making it a great place to unwind after a full day of sightseeing.

eats.name: Troubadour
eats.note: A popular bar/café which comes alive at night with daily live music, usually jazz. Can be very expensive, so you often see people sitting on nearby steps enjoying the music with drinks bought from the

eats.name: Beer Factory
eats.note: Despite its sterile sounding name, this place has a lovely courtyard out the back. Its real draw however is that it is possibly one of the cheapest places to get a beer in the old town. Some reasonabl

eats.name: Culture Club Revelin
eats.note: Dubrovnik's liveliest night spot, techno and other styles.

eats.name: Banje Beach Club
eats.note: Beach club, bar and Med-style restaurant by day, at night you can party in the nightclub. Great view, various kinds of music, popular DJs and beautiful atmosphere.

eats.name: Klub Orlando
eats.note: Dingy club, predominantly metal but seems to cater for anything deemed alternative. Cheap drink prices with occasional international touring acts, definitely in the minority as a tourist here.

eats.name: Lazareti
eats.note: House and techno music.

next.name: Cavtat
next.note: Cavtat and the Konavle Valley, immediately to the south

next.name: Mljet
next.note: Mljet is a green island with national park, lakes and monasteries.

next.name: Neum
next.note: Neum is the coastal town within Herzegovina that used to be a border crossing hassle, until the Pelješac Bridge bypassed it completely. It remains a low-tax shopping centre.

next.name: Međugorje
next.note: Međugorje on the road to Mostar has a large Catholic shrine.

next.name: Mostar
next.note: Mostar is about 3 hr away by bus, an easy day-trip. You really feel its Turkish heritage.

next.name: Sarajevo
next.note: Sarajevo the capital is a remarkable city, scarred by several centuries of conflict but nowadays safe and friendly.
